fixed_constraints: I50 aligns docs with shipped behavior across READMEs, index, ledger, coverage, plan, CLI guides, and fresh release notes, stripping proof, compatibility, obsolete-syntax, and unsupported-platform assertions.
Dated design material remains labeled plus linked rather than quietly recast as present authority; the frozen contract's own rule bars silent rewrites.
Release notes are missing entirely; signing, notarization, and upload persist as open gates with prepared commands, and provider quality stays unclaimed.
Closure demands verified contract-evidence links, exact pins and limits, a clean-machine install-to-run pass, and a full fifty-checkbox recount.
common.purpose: Resolve three I50 documentation design points for the Can tree: the REQUIREMENTS.md fate, the release-notes shape, and the docs index scope.

index_scope.background: Dated design links share the docs index with a status map and reading steps invoking live sketches, adjacent goldens, and a CAN registry, all gone.
facts: Its lower half already carries historical-incomplete labels, but the reading order still walks reviewers through removed sketch programs and golden gates.
Present authority rests in the task ledger, coverage mapping, evidence directories, and package READMEs, which the index fails to center.
Surgical relabeling preserves anchors while reconstruction endangers deep links from evidence and review notes pointing at today's headings.

release_notes_shape.background: Candidate release notes must capture shipped state, pins, open gates, install flow, and limits, either as a fresh implementation file or within the distribution guide.
facts: Install, upgrade, prepared signing, and the unsigned-release gate already live in distribution/README.md across I01/I02/I39 sections.
Root README, ledger, and evidence all point outward for release truth, yet no unified notes file joins version, pins, gates, and limits.
Task evidence belongs to implementation documents and shipping procedure to distribution documents, placing notes on the seam between audiences.

requirements_fate.background: Root REQUIREMENTS.md holds 288 lines of frozen v0.1 contract around decision tables, given/call evidence, revision pins, and CAN codes, all retired by the shipped compiler.
facts: Its freeze rule bans silent rewrites and admits tagged amendments only, outlawing any quiet in-place modernization.
Index plus root README still present it as the living contract and route readers through it toward deleted sketches.
Current tests, gates, and examples enforce none of its clauses; the ledger, coverage mapping, and evidence directories hold enforcement.
